newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Calliope closer to nickel refinery start-up.
newsitem.headline: Calliope closer to nickel refinery start-up.

text.p: Canada's Calliope Metals Corp has moved a step closer to establishing its A$316 million nickel/cobalt refinery in the Australian state of Queensland with ore supply agreements now in place with two established New Caledonian nickel mining companies.
Calliope had negotiated conditional long-term contracts for the supply of up to 1.5 million wet tonnes of lateritic ore annually, the company said in its listing prospectus.
Calliope will list soon on the Australian Stock Exchange under the code.
"Ore supplies are expected in the second quarter of 1999 with commissioning of the new refinery scheduled for the third quarter of 1999," Calliope managing director, Gavin Becker said on Wednesday.
Additional ore supplies were expected to be arranged to meet the project's full requirements, Becker told Reuters.

Initial ore supply of 660,000 dry tonnes a year had been secured from Ste de la Tontouta's orebodies in New Caledonia's Nakety region with an additional 330,000 tonnes annually agreed with Mai Kouaoua Mines SARL.

Becker said production from the refinery in the north Queensland city of Gladstone would benefit from "very, very positive signs" of an increasing world demand for nickel, reflecting its use in a burgeoning stainless steel industry.
About two-thirds of all nickel consumed was accounted for in stainless steel and alloy steel production, he said.
"In round terms an additional 30,000 tonnes a year in increased (nickel) consumption is expected. That is a Calliope every eight months," Becker said.
Calliope's refinery would use the pressure acid leach process with a planned production rate of 18,740 tonnes a year of nickel and 1,890 tonnes annually of cobalt.
"Calliope's business plan, importing the raw materials, adding value via state of the art technology and on-selling for export a high quality product, is rare in Australia," he said.

Following the local listing of its shares which expected early next week, Calliope would proceed with seeking development financing for the refinery which was scheduled to start construction later this year.
